title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Music-Practice Desk. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Music-Practice Desk
options.lineage: conservatory practice-desk notation culture — urtext editions, marked scores, tempo discipline
options.thesis: Your document is the score, the spoken sentence is the practice cursor, tempo is speed, and the desk remembers where you stopped.
options.viewport: Desktop app: deep-blue instrument rail with tempo dial, voice channels, and a passage list with minute counts; a bright white score panel shows the active sentence lifted in blue wash under a red practice cursor; one status band reads 'Movement II · 4:12 remaining'.
options.risk: Practice-desk warmth can drift into wood-and-lamplight nostalgia if materials go soft; commit to urtext blue and score white.

raised.raise: Grease-pencil ticks mark finished passages; a folded red flag marks where practice stopped.
One status band speaks one fact at a time — section name plus minutes remaining, set monumentally.
Sentence timings show as a real monospace data strip: start and end milliseconds, tabular.
Exactly one saturated active mark on screen at a time: the spoken sentence.
The work's title is set monumental — the piece being practiced, named like a composition.
The score panel is the one calm zone; instrument chrome may carry material energy, the text never does.

options.label: Annotated Manuscript
options.lineage: commonplace books, critical editions, highlighter culture
options.thesis: The page is the learner's own document, and the active sentence receives the newest annotation in real time.
options.viewport: Full-bleed document with a margin rail of live notes; the spoken sentence sits under a fresh highlighter stroke as playback moves.
options.risk: Highlighter-and-paper is exactly where most reading-product runs land — familiar and effective, not distinctive.

options.label: Cutting-Bench Select Rail
options.lineage: film editing benches — work prints, perforated rails, tape flags
options.thesis: The document is a work print on a perforated rail; sentences are frames; the stop point wears a folded tape flag.
options.viewport: Black bench with an orange perforated rail crossing at a fixed height; the active sentence punched white; finished trims hanging on pins below.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: scrub-to-frame is sentence-sync and resume-where-you-stopped is a real need. Holds clarity; identification is partial for students.
options.risk: Editorial-film language can feel foreign to study ritual, and a true-black ground costs reading comfort.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.lineage: international airport sign systems — Schiphol yellow bands, gate numerals
options.thesis: Sections are gates, the route stays highlighted band to band, and one status band tells you minutes remaining.
options.viewport: A yellow overhead band with monumental 'Movement II — 4:12' above document rows styled as gate panels with walking-time numerals.
options.case: Minutes-remaining is a real product fact and route-follow is read-along. Holds clarity; identification is partial — signage is about leaving, and here the destination is the text.
options.risk: Sustained reading inside terminal yellow can fatigue; the signage grammar must not colonize the document.

options.label: Data-Sublime Field
options.lineage: Ikeda datamatics — barcode fields, sine lattices, inversion
options.thesis: Speech timing rendered as a pure black-and-white data field: columns, numerals, one sine trace.
options.viewport: A wall of vertical bar columns with the active sentence as a single inverted frame.
options.case: Loses both axes: students do not identify with data-sublime installation grammar, and long-form reading in pure bars punishes comprehension.
options.kept: Tabular timestamp honesty — the timeline as first-class monospace data.

options.label: Paper-Fold Sequence
options.lineage: orizuru crane sequences — one sheet, thirty-two folds
options.thesis: The document progresses as fold states; sections are steps; one gold dot marks the active fold.
options.viewport: A vermilion field with a crease-pattern progress diagram beside the reading column.
options.case: Loses both axes: fold states decorate the progress idea but cannot carry highlighting or sync.
options.kept: One gold mark — a single active indicator, everything else calm.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.lineage: surreal type-worlds — letters as weather, words as landscape
options.thesis: Language behaves as matter: titles loom monumental while text threatens to scatter into weather.
options.viewport: A monumental document title over a body that reads as weather fronts.
options.case: Loses clarity badly: motion and transformation fight sustained comprehension, which is the product's whole job.
options.kept: Monumental title — the work named like an object at the top of the desk.

options.label: Street-Fair Hoarding
options.lineage: screenprinted festival hoardings — riso collage, torn deckle, letter-per-color
options.thesis: Every inch is print collage except one calm white panel — and that panel is the document.
options.viewport: A full-bleed collage plane with one floating white finder card holding the text.
options.case: Loses identification for serious study: event-poster energy gamifies a comprehension tool.
options.kept: One calm panel wins the page — the document is the only quiet zone.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What this category ships, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A white SaaS reader: centered hero, blue play button, three feature cards, zinc chrome.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
